subject: Week 37: pincer practice at every meal — open cup beats the sippy
bodyText:
This week
The pincer grasp — thumb and index finger — is emerging and refines fastest with daily practice; the CDC checks it at 12 months, so emerging now is ahead of the checkpoint, not a requirement. Self-feeding capacity is expanding: many infants this week can drink from an open cup with help, which beats a sippy for oral-motor development. Babble is picking up adult-like intonation, and a specific mama or dada is emerging for some.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Food and objects launched from the high chair — gravity experimentation, not defiance; it fades faster without an audience reaction.
- [monitor] No raking grasp or no progress toward picking up small foods — bring it to the 9-month visit.
- [monitor] Not imitating sounds or simple actions — same route: visit notes, not alarm.
- [call within 24h] Persistent illness that is not improving.
- [call now] Choking with no air movement — start infant back blows and chest thrusts and call 911; fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy — call now.

Enrichment opportunities
- Serve two-finger-size pieces at every meal and hand over pre-loaded spoons (yogurt, mashed potato). The mess is the training signal — daily self-feeding practice drives the pincer refinement the CDC checks at 12 months. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Offer an open cup with help at one meal a day and sketch the bottle exit: AAP guidance is off bottles entirely by 12 months, and open-cup practice is the ramp. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Contact certified ISR instructors before the window closes Feb 5 if pool or regular water exposure is in the family's future — Bay Area instructors book 6-12+ months out, and the evidence is case-series only, so treat it as drowning-risk mitigation, not enrichment. ISR instructor directory: https://www.infantswim.com/
- Keep live music daily — sing the same two songs at cleanup and bath. Active participation, not playback, is what moved pitch discrimination and prelinguistic gesture in the randomized trial (Gerry, Unrau and Trainor 2012). Gerry/Unrau/Trainor 2012 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — the window is open; attend or book this week. Iron rescreen, influenza #2 if first season, possible ASQ-3.
- Day 270 (Feb 5, 2027): ISR instructor-contact and Suzuki-waitlist windows close.
- Day 264-270 (Jan 30–Feb 5, 2027): first words consolidating — log anything that sounds referential.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Pulls to stand at furniture or your legs
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Time to switch to a lower crib mattress setting if not already.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pulls-to-stand/complete

- Babbles with inflection (sounds like speech)
  AAP window: day 240-330
  What to look for: Jargon. Pitch and rhythm of a sentence without recognizable words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/babbles-with-inflection/complete

- Explores objects by shaking, banging, throwing, dropping
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Systematic property exploration. Repetitive drops are research, not defiance.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/explores-objects-many-ways/complete

- Lets objects go voluntarily (drops on purpose)
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Controlled release — distinct from accidental dropping. Predecessor to throwing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/lets-objects-go-voluntarily/complete

- Pokes with index finger
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Isolated finger use. Predecessor to pointing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pokes-with-index/complete
